audit_findings.title: Known Azar distribution break is absent from the anchor and perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $19 million Q2 2026 Azar revenue decline and $25.2 million trade-name impairment; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor is capitalized without reflecting Azar's post-removal revenue and margin deterioration.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 22, 2026, Apple removed the Azar app from the Apple App Store.
audit_findings.explanation: The distribution break was real, and Q2 results demonstrate lower revenue. However, Apple reinstated a modified Azar app on April 6, 2026, so permanent loss is not established. The impairment is noncash and does not itself reduce OE. The record does not isolate Azar's post-reinstatement cash margin, preventing a materiality determination.
audit_findings.action: Replace Azar's FY2025 contribution with post-reinstatement revenue and cash-margin evidence through June 2026, then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Temporary Google fee savings may be capitalized as permanent earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary in-app purchase fee savings elevate the OE anchor and projected margins if capitalized beyond the Q1 2027 partnership expiry.
audit_findings.evidence: If Google does not reduce its standard in-app purchase fees, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, before that partnership expires, we expect that the fees paid to Google for transactions processed either through their in-app payment system or through alternative payment options on Android, will increase.
audit_findings.explanation: The partnership-specific FY2025 benefit is not separately filed. Total in-app purchase fees fell $9.5 million in FY2025, and computed H1 2026 segment fees fell $60.1 million year over year, but those changes also reflect alternative-payment migration and cannot be attributed to Google. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 and H1 2026 Google-partnership benefit and contractual post-Q1 2027 fee schedule, then rerun OE with normalized fees.

audit_findings.title: Near-term operating trajectory conflicts with immediate positive-growth cases
audit_findings.magnitude: $77.7 million FY2025 Tinder direct-revenue decline (4%) and $22.9 million H1 2026 constant-FX decline (3%); value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The finding affects the first-year OE path and the 2% and 4% growth assumptions, which are then compounded and carried into terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Tinder expects revenue to decrease in 2026 at a similar rate to the decrease in 2025, as these features and investments are tested and implemented.
audit_findings.explanation: Tinder represented approximately 53% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, making its continued decline reasonably capable of changing scenario values. H1 2026 consolidated Adjusted EBITDA improved despite weak revenue, but that improvement includes cost reductions, lower platform fees, and easier legal-expense comparisons; it does not validate immediate durable OE growth. Terminal value is about 49%-50% of the positive-growth cases, increasing the importance of a reconciled path.
audit_findings.action: Build annual 2026-2030 OE by segment using filed revenue trends, sustainable margins, Azar effects, and normalized platform fees, then rerun the base and bull cases.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor may retain material one-off settlements and restructuring costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.5 million of identified settlements plus a $9.9 million year-over-year severance increase; settlements equal 12.1% of the $618.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained as recurring expenses, these charges reduce the FY2025 OE anchor and every forecast year's cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: General and administrative expense increased primarily due to (i) a legal settlement at Tinder in the amount of $60.5 million, (ii) a settlement with the FTC in the amount of $14.0 million related to certain E&E applications, and (iii) an increase in severance expense of $9.9 million primarily within Corporate and Unallocated Costs and E&E.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges are demonstrated FY2025 expenses, but their treatment in the OE bridge and the appropriate recurring legal and restructuring allowance remain unresolved. The identified settlements alone are large relative to the anchor and therefore reasonably capable of changing scenario values. This does not establish that the entire amount should be added back.
audit_findings.action: Trace each charge and its tax effect through the OE bridge, establish a supported recurring legal and restructuring allowance, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Dilution ceiling mixes economically inconsistent claim states
audit_findings.magnitude: 19.2 million shares; removing all 12.1 million warrant shares and 7.1 million 2030 conversion shares would raise the bull value only from $37.27 to approximately $40.17, still below the $41.86 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The inconsistency inflates fully diluted shares while OE retains exchangeable-note interest; warrant exercise proceeds are also omitted.
audit_findings.evidence: The Exchangeable Notes Warrants have a dilutive effect on the Company’s common stock to the extent that the market price per share of the Company’s common stock exceeds their respective strike prices.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied denominator conservatively includes warrants with strikes near $130 and 2030 conversion shares despite a valuation-date price of $41.86. Even the maximal denominator-only correction reduces shares from 266.251 million to 247.051 million and leaves the highest scenario below market. The inconsistency affects reported value per share but not the valuation conclusion at the supplied price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun coherent debt-outstanding and conversion cases, using treasury-stock treatment for warrants and adding back after-tax interest only in the conversion case.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved privacy exposure is a potential claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.1 million provision, approximately $0.03 per share and 0.10% of the $8,961 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time regulatory payment belongs in the equity bridge or the period's OE rather than being ignored.
audit_findings.evidence: Our consolidated financial statements do not reflect any provision for a loss with respect to this matter, as we do not believe there is a probable likelihood of an unfavorable outcome.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing supersedes the earlier unreserved $0-$60 million range: the DPC proposed an €8-€11 million fine and Match recorded a $9.1 million provision. Deducting $9.1 million from equity changes value by only about three cents per share, which is not material relative to the $33.66 base value or $41.86 market price.
audit_findings.action: Update the bridge for the $9.1 million provision and confirm the final DPC decision and payment before closing the finding.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $319.5 million for FY2022 and $30.6 million for FY2024 as supplied; FY2025 anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A demonstrated to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE; only an FY2025 adjustment can directly raise the binding latest-year anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $319.5m (78.0% of filed D&A); FY2024 $30.6m (18.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A expensed is conservative rather than a demonstrated overvaluation. Correcting the supplied FY2022 and FY2024 amounts alone would not change the current anchor because the $618.2 million FY2025 actual already binds below the $796 million trend. The record does not establish whether FY2025 contains an eligible residual or its amount, so a possible understatement remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2025 residual D&A from filed asset and amortization schedules; rerun only the supported eligible portion, and revisit historical years only if the anchor methodology changes.
